On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Here every submission is a program instead of a grid. To submit, write a Python function transform(grid) that
returns the output grid for an input of this task, in one ```python block using only the standard library, and end
your reply with {"action": "submit"}. Your program is run on the test input and its output is submitted. Before that
it is checked, at no cost, on every demonstration pair you have for this task, and a failure is reported to you;
after 3 failed checks in an instance, a program's output is submitted without a check. A program that reproduces all
the pairs you have is kept for the task: when the task returns, it is run on the new test input first and its output
is submitted.

```python
def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter

    base = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == base for v in grid[r]) < w / 2]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == base for r in range(h)) < h / 2]

    # The ordinary separator color is the most common non-interior color.
    sep = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != base).most_common(1)[0][0]

    def marked_at(r, c):
        return grid[r][c] != base and grid[r][c] != sep

    row_lines = [r for r in row_lines if any(marked_at(r, c) for c in col_lines)]
    col_lines = [c for c in col_lines if any(marked_at(r, c) for r in row_lines)]

    out = []
    for r1, r2 in zip(row_lines, row_lines[1:]):
        line = []
        for c1, c2 in zip(col_lines, col_lines[1:]):
            a, b = grid[r1][c1], grid[r1][c2]
            c, d = grid[r2][c1], grid[r2][c2]
            if a == b == c == d and a != base and a != sep:
                line.append(a)
            else:
                line.append(base)
        out.append(line)
    return out
```

```python
def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # The fill color is the most frequent row-wise majority color.
    row_majorities = [Counter(row).most_common(1)[0][0] for row in grid]
    base = Counter(row_majorities).most_common(1)[0][0]

    nonbase = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != base)
    sep = nonbase.most_common(1)[0][0]

    rows = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == base for v in grid[r]) < w / 2]
    cols = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == base for r in range(h)) < h / 2]

    def marked(r, c):
        return grid[r][c] != base and grid[r][c] != sep

    rows = [r for r in rows if any(marked(r, c) for c in cols)]
    cols = [c for c in cols if any(marked(r, c) for r in rows)]
    rows = [r for r in rows if any(marked(r, c) for c in cols)]

    return [
        [
            grid[r1][c1]
            if grid[r1][c1] == grid[r1][c2] == grid[r2][c1] == grid[r2][c2]
            and marked(r1, c1)
            else base
            for c1, c2 in zip(cols, cols[1:])
        ]
        for r1, r2 in zip(rows, rows[1:])
    ]
```
